1.modern-en: Beatrice greets the returning soldiers by asking the messenger after 'Signor Mountanto' and trades insults with Benedick as soon as he is in earshot.

4.modern-en: Beatrice attends the masked ball and lets Benedick, disguised, deliver his own bad reputation to her face.

6.modern-en: Beatrice is mentioned in Don Pedro's scheme to trick her and Benedick into loving each other.

7.modern-en: Beatrice is set up by Hero and Ursula to overhear that Benedick is dying of love for her, and she resolves on the spot to deserve him.

8.modern-en: Beatrice is teased by the men for her sudden change of mood.

12.modern-en: Beatrice stays behind after Hero's denunciation, weeps with her cousin, and asks Benedick to kill Claudio.

14.modern-en: Beatrice meets Benedick after the challenge has been issued and they confess their love between sentences about Hero's disgrace.

17.modern-en: Beatrice marries Benedick at the closing wedding, claiming to her last line that she takes him only out of pity.

epithet.en: A young lord of Padua, friend to Don Pedro and Claudio

1.modern-en: Benedick spars with Beatrice on first arrival and announces that no woman alive will marry him.

4.modern-en: Benedick attends the masked ball, hears Beatrice describe him as 'the prince's jester' to his masked face, and is humiliated by it.

5.modern-en: Benedick complains to Don Pedro about Beatrice and overhears Claudio's worry about Don John's plot.

6.modern-en: Benedick is lured into the garden so the others can fake a conversation about Beatrice's hidden love for him.

8.modern-en: Benedick reappears beardless and lovesick, and the men can hardly keep their faces straight.

12.modern-en: Benedick stays with Beatrice after the failed wedding and promises, at her demand, to challenge Claudio.

14.modern-en: Benedick delivers his challenge to Claudio and Don Pedro and quietly takes his leave of their company.

15.modern-en: Benedick struggles to write a love poem to Beatrice in the garden and gives up.

17.modern-en: Benedick proposes to Beatrice, calls for music and a dance, and ends the play married.

epithet.en: A young Florentine lord in Don Pedro's company

1.modern-en: Claudio falls in love with Hero on first sight and asks Benedick whether she is the sweetest lady he ever saw.

4.modern-en: Claudio is briefly persuaded at the masked ball that Don Pedro has wooed Hero for himself.

5.modern-en: Claudio receives the news that Hero is to be his and is congratulated by Don Pedro.

6.modern-en: Claudio takes part in the orchard scheme to trick Benedick into falling in love with Beatrice.

8.modern-en: Claudio is shown the staged window scene by Don John and accepts it as proof of Hero's infidelity.

12.modern-en: Claudio rejects Hero at the altar with the harshest language he can find and stalks out of the church with Don Pedro.

14.modern-en: Claudio refuses Benedick's challenge as a joke and laughs off Leonato's accusations until the watch presents the truth.

16.modern-en: Claudio comes to Hero's supposed tomb at night, hangs an epitaph, and accepts Leonato's offer of his niece in penance.

17.modern-en: Claudio is brought to a masked bride who turns out to be Hero alive, and marries her on the spot.

1.modern-en: Hero greets the returning soldiers in the company of her father and her cousin, the silent foil to Beatrice's wit.

4.modern-en: Hero is danced with at the masked ball by Don Pedro acting on Claudio's behalf, and consents to the match.

7.modern-en: Hero stages the second half of the matchmaking scheme by letting Beatrice overhear her praise Benedick.

10.modern-en: Hero dresses for the wedding while her women tease her about her wedding-night fears.

12.modern-en: Hero is denounced at the altar by Claudio, faints, and is left for dead by her father.

16.modern-en: Hero is mourned at the tomb by Claudio, who does not yet know she lives.

17.modern-en: Hero unmasks at the second wedding as the supposed niece, and is married to a repentant Claudio.

epithet.en: Prince of Aragon, leader of the returning soldiers

1.modern-en: Don Pedro arrives at Leonato's house after the war, hears of Claudio's love for Hero, and offers to woo her for him.

4.modern-en: Don Pedro stages the wooing at the masked ball, securing Hero for Claudio.

5.modern-en: Don Pedro presents Hero to Claudio and proposes the scheme to bring Beatrice and Benedick together.

6.modern-en: Don Pedro stages the orchard talk so Benedick will overhear that Beatrice loves him.

8.modern-en: Don Pedro is shown the false window scene by Don John and is convinced of Hero's guilt.

12.modern-en: Don Pedro stands at the altar with Claudio and joins in the public denunciation of Hero.

14.modern-en: Don Pedro takes Benedick's challenge as a joke and is brought up short by the watch's revelation.

17.modern-en: Don Pedro is the only one not paired off in the closing dance; he is gently mocked for it by Benedick.

epithet.en: Don Pedro's illegitimate brother, the play's villain

1.modern-en: Don John is presented at Leonato's house as the recently defeated, recently reconciled brother of Don Pedro.

3.modern-en: Don John tells his henchmen Conrade and Borachio that he intends to make trouble for Claudio's match with Hero.

4.modern-en: Don John deceives Claudio at the masked ball into briefly believing Don Pedro has stolen Hero for himself.

5.modern-en: Don John listens to Borachio's plan to stage a fake assignation at Hero's window and approves it.

8.modern-en: Don John brings Claudio and Don Pedro to witness the staged scene at the window and confirms his report.

12.modern-en: Don John attends the wedding to enjoy the result of his trick, then slips out of Messina.

epithet.en: Governor of Messina, Hero's father, Beatrice's uncle

1.modern-en: Leonato welcomes Don Pedro's company back to Messina and presides over the introductions and banter.

4.modern-en: Leonato accepts Claudio's offer for Hero at the masked ball and joins the matchmaking for Beatrice.

6.modern-en: Leonato plays his part in the orchard trick on Benedick, doing his best to look serious about Beatrice's hidden love.

8.modern-en: Leonato is told by Don Pedro and Claudio at the door that they have something to show him before the wedding.

11.modern-en: Leonato is interrupted by Dogberry's incomprehensible report on the morning of the wedding and dismisses him without listening.

12.modern-en: Leonato hears his daughter denounced at the altar and, broken, wishes her dead at his feet.

14.modern-en: Leonato confronts Claudio in the street and challenges him, then receives the watch's prisoners and learns the truth.

15.modern-en: Leonato is briefly seen ordering the next day's funeral arrangements.

17.modern-en: Leonato presides over the unmasking of Hero and the double wedding.

9.modern-en: Dogberry briefs his watch on their duties with comically garbled instructions and orders them to sleep on their posts if necessary.

11.modern-en: Dogberry comes to Leonato with news of the arrest and is sent away because Leonato has no time to follow his syntax.

13.modern-en: Dogberry examines Borachio and Conrade in the prison with a sexton, insists on being recorded as an ass, and elicits the confession.

14.modern-en: Dogberry brings the bound prisoners to Don Pedro and Claudio in the street and lays out the case.

3.modern-en: Borachio is at the secret meeting where Don John resolves to spoil Claudio's match.

5.modern-en: Borachio lays out the plan to put on Hero's clothes for a tryst with him at her window while Claudio watches from a distance.

9.modern-en: Borachio brags drunkenly in the street to Conrade about the trick, and is overheard by the watch.

13.modern-en: Borachio is examined by Dogberry in the prison and confesses the conspiracy in detail.

14.modern-en: Borachio confesses publicly to Don Pedro and Claudio that the window scene was staged.

7.modern-en: Margaret carries the bait that brings Beatrice into the garden to overhear Hero and Ursula.

10.modern-en: Margaret jokes with Hero about her wedding clothes as the bride dresses.

15.modern-en: Margaret trades wit with Benedick at the garden gate as he waits to meet Beatrice.
